design_rationale:
DOSSIER — task 0 (round 2; cataract surgery package, late patient move, 40% charity award; root estimate_ext_surgical_balance)

1. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[4,5,5]. estimate_ext_surgical_balance 4 factors (root), estimate_ext_surgical_deposit 5, estimate_ext_late_change_fee 5.

2. Why a good test. Dale Strehlow asks only to "pay what Riverbend needs from you before the surgery". The agent must read the surgical pre-service-balance rule and find its two prerequisite sentences ("The pre-service balance is fixed only after the booking carries its initial deposit collection." and the late-change-fee sentence), see that no collection and no retained fee stand, recognise from the appointment records that the procedure slot was cancelled by the patient 4 days before it while the booking continued at a new date, read from the fee rule that "The late-change fee is retained only once an initial deposit collection stands on the surgery booking.", and compute three amounts from the estimate lines and deposits, the approved assistance case, the emergency-room charge lines and the appointment fees. Every figure for this charity-approved patient is figured on the award-discounted package price; the premium toric lens is a patient-elected upgrade outside the package and outside the award.

3. Scope. Claimed: estimate_ext_surgical_deposit, estimate_ext_late_change_fee, estimate_ext_surgical_balance; tools pay_surgery_package_deposit_c16ec91c (user), retain_late_change_fee_0cd5c1f6 (agent), pay_surgery_package_balance_24461a4e (user). Task 1 holds the maternity pair; scopes disjoint, union = all five.

4. Problem-tree card. Edges (all value_input on deposits_held, all state form):
- balance <- deposit: "The pre-service balance is fixed only after the booking carries its initial deposit collection." False at the opening: deposit_held_usd 0.00, only line rows. Only pay_surgery_package_deposit writes an INITIAL_DEPOSIT collection on a surgery estimate.
- balance <- fee: "The pre-service balance is not fixed until the booking shows a retained late-change fee entry for its late patient move, where it has one; a booking carries at most one such entry." (the late patient move is defined by one sentence carried verbatim in both the fee rule and the balance rule) — a record test, one entry per booking, matching the fee rule's "a booking carries at most one late-change fee" (no reference to another policy's figure). False: slot 2026-10-08 cancelled by the patient 2026-10-04, version 2 for 2026-11-05, no stay charge on 2026-10-04, no fee row. Only retain_late_change_fee writes that row.
- fee <- deposit: "The late-change fee is retained only once an initial deposit collection stands on the surgery booking."
- Directions: affirmative, negated, affirmative. Order deposit (11) -> fee (13) -> balance (15), fully ordered.
- Deletion sensitivity: skip deposit -> balance 3144.20 and fee capped 0.00; skip fee -> balance not fixed (0.00).

5. Base-invariant card. Subjects estimate_deposit_collected (estimate_package_pricing, no structured eligibility -> policy_scope) and estimate_cancellation_fee_retained (estimate_cancellation_and_deposit_refund; one_refund_per_deposit applies to refunds -> policy_scope). No time eligibility realised. Overwrites: deposit and balance clauses of package pricing, each replaced_by restating the clause for other tiers and naming the maternity sibling; the fee retires the late-cancellation clause for moves only, restating it for cancellations; the base full-refund sentence stays in force and the fee's lateness test is that same calendar-day test (fewer than the full-refund days, counting back from the slot date).

6. Business-object card. Target estimate 13e359ed-ae3b-401d-9d25-bf03c933ea68. Package price = version-2 lines with code 66984, roles CONVENING_FACILITY 2480.00 and CONVENING_PROFESSIONAL 900.00 = 3380.00 (the schedule price). Implant lines read only by code: V2787 1150.00. Excluded: anesthesia co-provider 00142. The fee is kept from the single deposit collection created at step 11.

7. Factor card (tier / evidence / figure under the factor's baseline).
Deposit (gold 1825.20; all-baseline 1690.00):
- aid_basis (method, cross-difficulty assist, multi-source: approved AND covers 2026-11-05): 40% -> base 2028.00; baseline 3042.00.
- lead_share_pct: 16 days to surgery -> 75%; baseline 1318.20.
- late_deposit_points: 36 days since scheduling -> +5; baseline 1723.80.
- moved_booking_points: two versions -> +5; baseline 1723.80.
- missed_visit_points (visit): one fee 2026-05-19, near-miss 2025-03-11 outside 12 months -> +5; baseline 1723.80.
Fee (gold 19.01; all-baseline 150.00):
- fee_basis (method): 3380.00 -> max(150.00, 5%) = 169.00; baseline 16.88.
- notice_share: 4 days -> 0.50; baseline 38.03.
- acute_care_share (cross-difficulty encounter; single-source since round 3): ER 2026-10-03, the day before the change date -> 0.50; baseline 38.03.
- postponement_share: 28 days -> 0.75; baseline 25.35.
- aid_fee_share (cross-difficulty assist): 0.60; baseline 31.69.
Balance (gold 1287.31; all-baseline 1573.81):
- aid_price (method, cross-difficulty assist, multi-source): 2028.00; baseline 2639.31.
- implant_share: premium lens listed -> whole 1150.00; baseline 137.31.
- early_credit_pct: 16 days -> 1% = 33.80; baseline 1321.11.
- full_credit_pct: deposit posted today -> 1.5% = 50.70; baseline 1338.01.
Method all-pairs (XF C14): aid {price x (100-d)/100 | min(price, cap - used) | price}: tariff input vs min op + cap inputs vs identity; distinguishing price 3380.00, d 40, cap 1000.00, used 0 -> 2028.00 / 1000.00 / 3380.00. fee_basis {flat + 1% x price | max(flat, 5% x price) | flat}: add vs max vs constant; schedule prices 7450/5875/5290 -> 224.50/208.75/202.90, 3380 -> 169.00, 1640 -> 150.00 (distinct per tier, monotone).

8. Seed rationale (band 55: phone 9205550512, MRN RB55204817, ssn 5372). A2 ED 2026-10-03: gross 1878.00, 45% uninsured discount 845.10, first statement 2026-10-12 (1032.90), award applied 2026-10-14 with the assist formula: AGB 34.6% x 1878.00 = 649.79, liability 649.79 x 0.60 = 389.87, charity 1032.90 - 389.87 = 643.03, balance 389.87. Assist case: application 2026-10-09 at the financial counselor (A2 had no statement yet, so inside the period), pay stubs and residency accepted 2026-10-13, approved 2026-10-14 at the 40% tier (340.0% FPL, no BadgerCare screening required on that tier), award 2025-10-09 (application minus 365) to 2027-04-14 (determination plus 6 months), charity_applied_total 643.03; no other encounter falls in the award window. Visit: procedure slot 2026-10-08 booked 2026-09-14, cancelled by the patient 2026-10-04 (93 hours, above the visit charter's 72-hour late window, so no visit fee), reminders at 7 days; replacement slot 2026-11-05; ophthalmology consult no-show 2026-05-19 (50.00 assessed, waived first occurrence); primary-care no-show 2025-03-11 (25.00, waived). Estimate: two versions of four lines; the V2787 line is the expected actual charge 2300.00 less the 50% outpatient-surgery uninsured discount.

9. Persona. Short practical sentences; volunteers the goal and that he pays himself; identity on request; the ER visit only if asked why the date moved, the award only if asked about assistance; pays exactly what he is told; accepts the fee after it is explained; closes when told the surgery payment went through.

10. Standard solution. Reads 0-9 (profile, verification, estimate, lines, assistance case and activity, appointments and fees, hospital account and activity); 10-11 patient pays 1825.20; 12-13 agent keeps 19.01 from that collection; 14-15 patient pays 1287.31.

11. Verification (scratch verify.py / v_all.py on the handling-time worlds): figures as in section 7; gate outputs in the difficulty worklog.

12. Easily got wrong: the estimate total 5210.00 as the package price; applying the award to the premium lens; the flat 150.00 fee; refunding instead of keeping (it is a move); balance before fee; fee before deposit.

13. Draft recomputation from the visible rules, finder outputs and persona gives the same three writes and amounts.

14. Round-2 revisions (audit revision_1): CG-1 calendar-day lateness; CG-2 scope gate on the later version's date and furnish date; CG-3 carve-outs (hospital stay, 100% award or used-up cap, nothing left to pay) by record tests; CG-4 half-up rounding in compute; CG-6/T0-F2 implants by listed codes and the world moved to a premium toric lens; CG-7 fee_basis tiers distinct; CG-8/T0-F1 statement and rebooking reserves removed; CG-9/T0-F3 docstrings without ordering words or another write's receipt; collections_security removed (501(r) ECA class); the award applied to every pre-service figure and to the fee.


15. Round-3 revisions (audit revision_2): R2-1 the award records (case, tier, cap, liability booked, cap left, period and coverage) and the implant total are plain shared bindings, each defined once in the rule ('the patient\'s award ... covers ... cap left'; 'the implant total is ...'); the award factors keep only the tier discount read and their ladder, the implant factor only the line-presence counts; the carve-out reads the award's tier name and cap left, never a factor binding. R2-2 the late-change fee keeps at most one fee per booking (a retained entry already standing puts a later move outside the fee rule), the fee reads the first patient-cancelled slot the appointment record lists, and the balance's prerequisite sentence and edge condition name that same slot and the same one-entry state. R2-3 acute_care_share is a single-source ladder on the latest emergency room charge date (the hospital-stay test stays only in the scope carve-out). Gold unchanged: 1825.20 / 19.01 / 1287.31; factor_sensitivity unchanged.

16. Round-4 revision (audit revision_3, R3-1): the late patient move is now one record-test sentence carried verbatim in both the fee rule and the balance rule (first-listed patient-cancelled procedure slot; cancelled on or before the slot date and fewer calendar days before it than the full-refund days; estimate not cancelled; current version a later version furnished on or after the cancellation date with a different service date; no 0120/0762 charge on the cancellation date). The fee rule's scope refers to that term; the balance waits on a retained fee entry "for its late patient move, where it has one", and its compute returns no amount (0.00) while a late patient move lacks its entry. A world whose version predates the cancellation (2026-10-03 vs 2026-10-04) has no late patient move: no fee and no wait, the balance is fixed. Gold unchanged: 1825.20 / 19.01 / 1287.31; the skip-fee figure changed from 1268.30 to not fixed (0.00).

17. Round-5 revision (renderer scan render_r1): the implant total is now one of the implant factor's own bindings and is defined inside the factor's sentence ("Implant share of the pre-service balance: the implant total is ...; when a premium intraocular lens line ... the whole implant total is added; ..."); the factor decides the implant amount (share x total), which the balance figure adds, so no plain binding reads a factor-internal binding. The booking-history points state the empty case ("one, or none recorded, adds none"). The tool bodies record amounts with a half-up helper matching their docstrings (docstrings unchanged). Gold unchanged: 1825.20 / 19.01 / 1287.31; factor_sensitivity unchanged (implant_share baseline 137.31).
user_scenario: You are Dale Strehlow, a 58-year-old self-employed roofing contractor from Appleton, Wisconsin, calling Riverbend's Good Faith & Price Estimates desk on a Tuesday morning. You have no health insurance and booked Riverbend's self-pay package price for cataract surgery on your right eye at the Riverbend Surgery & Imaging Center in Grand Chute, with the toric lens your eye doctor recommended for your astigmatism; the surgery is now set for November 5, 2026. You talk in short, practical sentences and want the thing settled in one call. You open by saying you are calling about your cataract surgery package and that you want to pay what Riverbend needs from you before the surgery, today, so nothing is hanging over you on surgery day; you will pay with your own card and enter it yourself. When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Dale Strehlow, and your phone number, 9205550512. When the agent asks you to confirm your identity, you give your date of birth, 1968-03-14, and then the medical record number printed on your paperwork, RB55204817, one at a time as asked. You do not know the package price breakdown, what has or has not been paid on it, or how Riverbend figures any amount; if the agent asks what you think you owe, you say you do not have a number and want them to tell you. Only if the agent asks whether you have financial assistance do you say a financial counselor helped you apply after your emergency room visit and you got an approval letter in the mail last week. Only if the agent asks why the surgery date changed do you explain that you ended up in the Neenah emergency room on October 3 with bronchitis and called the surgeon's office on October 4 to push the surgery back. If the agent asks how you will pay, it is your Visa card. Whenever the agent tells you an amount and hands a payment step over to you, you make that payment yourself for exactly the amount the agent gave you, and then read back the confirmation number you were given. If the agent explains that Riverbend keeps a fee out of what you have paid because you moved the date, you grumble briefly that you figured there would be something and tell them to go ahead. When the agent tells you the payment for the surgery has gone through and that nothing more is due from you before November 5, you thank them and end the call. You do not bring up anything else on your own, you do not ask for documents or receipts to be sent anywhere, and you never correct or second-guess the agent's figures.
